analyticsSettings.title: Analytics Settings
analyticsSettings.description: Visitor statistics for the public portal via Cloudflare Web Analytics.
analyticsSettings.overviewDesc: Cloudflare Web Analytics is a free, privacy-first, cookie-free traffic analytics service. The portal (apps/web) loads it through a single static JavaScript beacon embedded at build time — no Workers, KV or D1 involved, so the deployment stays pure static hosting.
analyticsSettings.beaconNote: Only the public portal (apps/web) loads the beacon; this admin console and the JBrowse app do not.
analyticsSettings.configDesc: The beacon token is a VITE_* variable injected at BUILD time into the portal HTML. This page is a documentation-only interface: it does not store the token, does not call the backend, and cannot change the running site.
analyticsSettings.envVarHelp: Set it in the Cloudflare Pages project "soymutdb-web" → Settings → Environment variables, for both Production and Preview. Values cannot be read back from the dashboard after saving.
analyticsSettings.step1Desc: Cloudflare Dashboard → Analytics & Logs → Web Analytics → Add a site. Pick the portal domain (e.g. www.example.com). No DNS/proxy change is required — the beacon works on any static host.
analyticsSettings.step2Desc: Open the installation snippet of the new site and copy the token from data-cf-beacon (a short hex string).
analyticsSettings.step3Desc: In the soymutdb-web Pages project: Settings → Environment variables → Add variable VITE_CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN with the token value (Production and Preview), then redeploy.
analyticsSettings.step4Desc: Trigger a new production deployment so the token is baked into the built index.html. Older deployments created before the variable was added contain no beacon.
analyticsSettings.step5Desc: Open the portal and view the page source: it should contain static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js. Traffic then appears in Cloudflare Dashboard → Web Analytics (may take a few minutes).
analyticsSettings.statusDesc: The token is injected into the portal HTML at build time, so this page cannot detect the current injection state at runtime (the admin bundle never carries the value). Use the checks below instead.
analyticsSettings.statusHint1: Open the portal in a browser → View page source (Ctrl/Cmd+U) → search for "cloudflareinsights". Found means the beacon is injected in the current deployment.
analyticsSettings.statusHint2: Or check Cloudflare Dashboard → Web Analytics: if the site shows traffic shortly after a deployment, the beacon is working.
analyticsSettings.legacyDesc: The native PostgreSQL analytics endpoints (/analytics, /stats) and the portal /analytics page remain available for on-site data; Cloudflare Web Analytics is the primary visitor-statistics channel.
analyticsSettings.loadError: Analytics is unavailable for this deployment: the summary endpoint could not be reached. No placeholder numbers are shown.

help.title: Help Center
help.subtitle: Find answers and learn how to use SoyMutDB
help.step1: Pick a genome assembly. Every search, download and locus belongs to exactly one assembly, so the same identifier can look different across v4 and v5.
help.step2: Search by gene ID, mutant public ID, or a genomic region. Results carry the chromosome, coordinates, and the release they were read from.
help.step3: Open a gene or mutant line for the full record, then continue into JBrowse 2, downloads, or the research tools.

q1.q: Why does a gene ID return different coordinates in another assembly?
q1.a: Coordinates are assembly-scoped. v4 and v5 are separate coordinate namespaces, so a result always reports the assembly it came from instead of being merged.

q2.q: Which release am I looking at?
q2.a: The release is shown in the page header and pinned on every request, so a page rendered from one release never mixes rows from another.

q3.q: Can I search with an internal record identifier?
q3.a: No. Public searches accept public identifiers only; internal identifiers are not disclosed, and an unknown one is treated exactly like a released record that does not exist.

q4.a: The downloads page issues short-lived presigned URLs scoped to your visibility and the active release.

q5.q: What do the research tools need?
q5.a: Sequence fetch, expression patterns and enrichment all require an explicit assembly, because a region or a gene list is otherwise ambiguous.

q6.q: How often is the data updated?
q6.a: Release versions and publication dates are announced on the News and Downloads pages. SoyMutDB does not promise a fixed release cadence on this Help page.

faq1.q: How do I search for a gene?
faq1.a: Use the search bar at the top of any page, or visit the Genes page to filter by chromosome, biotype, or keyword. Gene IDs follow the Glyma.01G000100 format.

faq2.q: How do I download variant data?
faq2.a: Visit the Downloads page for the files currently published for a release. Check each item's format, assembly, release, and provenance metadata before using it in an analysis.

faq3.a: Open the Seed Request page to see whether requests are currently enabled and to review the eligibility and distribution terms shown during submission.

faq4.a: Use the citation and provenance metadata published with the exact data release you used. A journal citation or DOI is shown only after it has been verified by the project maintainers.

faq5.a: The assembly is part of the search, record, browser, and download context. Confirm the displayed assembly before comparing or combining genomic coordinates.

faq6.q: How often is the data updated?
faq6.a: Release versions and publication dates are announced on the News and Downloads pages. SoyMutDB does not promise a fixed release cadence on this Help page.
